tools.name: is_hiring
tools.description: WHEN an agent already holds a company and needs to qualify it -- the cheap gate before spending a richer call. ATS/board-only and freshness-floored. Takes the integer `company_id` from an earlier result, not a company name or domain. company_id=1234 -> is_hiring true, open_req_count 7, coverage_stat

tools.name: hiring_pulse
tools.description:
A company's hiring velocity/direction/momentum in one call --

    "crawling"}` instead of a synchronous body, same as the REST route.

tools.name: pre_action_brief
tools.description:
The motion atoms + history primitives pre-joined into one
    bounded, compact call -- dual-metered via `max_age`. Cold returns
    `{job_id, status: "crawling"}`, same as the REST route.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description:
The `since=cursor` diff feed -- ledger events with `event_seq >
    since`, plus a `next_cursor`. Meters one `change` unit per event
    returned, independent of poll count. A free-tier caller is
    freshness-floored, the same as every other free-tier read. `limit` is
    bounded: an oversized page

tools.name: register_webhook
tools.description:
Register the delivery target a watch fires to, and get back the
    `webhook_endpoint_id` `watch_company` needs -- call this first if you
    do not already hold one. Idempotent: registering the same `url` twice
    returns the same id, so retrying is safe and never leaves you with two
    endpoints

tools.name: watch_company

    `webhook_endpoint_id` must belong to the same customer as the
    authenticated key. Meters one `watch` unit.

tools.name: write_outcome
tools.description:
Write back a conversion outcome for `company_id` -- the
    label-flywheel substrate. Appends to `outcome_labels` scoped to the
    caller's own customer.

    Plane session only: `outcome_labels` is plane-owned (Phase 1 dropped its
    one foreign key into the corpus) and this tool reads no corpus

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_changes, register_webhook · Private data: who_is_hiring_for, register_webhook · Public sink: register_webhook, watch_company.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_changes, register_webhook · Private data: who_is_hiring_for, register_webhook · Public sink: register_webhook, watch_company

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "watch_company" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
